ZHU 𒌉𒎌 𒆍𒀭𒊏 𒆠𒊭 𒀀𒈾 𒊑𒂊𒋗𒋾
𒋗𒇻𒆪 𒀭𒀀 𒍢𒅔𒁲 𒅇 𒄵𒋼
𒍪𒀪𒌑𒍪 𒌑𒉺𒄭𒅕, turi Babel-ki sa ana
resuti suluku ana ẓindi va birte zuhuzu upaḥir; the young men of Babylon
who at the head went, to strong chains and bonds I brought.—Black St. iv. 32.
These passages should explain each other, but any explanation I can suggest
is unsatisfactory; the chains and bonds may be simply guarantees and obligations,
because the conclusion which follows the last quoted passage states that the writer
aggregated these men to the people of Babylon, under restrictions.
ZHI 𒍝𒀪𒄿𒊑, za'iri; Enemies. Heb. צור or צָרַר.

𒈜𒁉𒅀 𒅈𒋫𒆏, ina rukub taḥa̧ẓi-ya ẓirti
ṣapinat ẓairi ina uqqum labbi-ya artakab; in my lofty war-chariot, the
sweeper of enemies, in the vengeance of my heart I drove.—Sen. T. v. 57.
¶ In the following passage I am inclined to compare za'iri with צָעִיר, "small,
weak:"—
𒆷 𒈠𒄀𒊑 𒀀𒈾𒅈 𒀝 𒈪
𒍝𒀪𒄿𒊑 𒈠𒁕 𒍑𒋼 𒅆
𒉌𒌨𒍑𒋫 𒄠𒈪𒄴, la magiri anar akvi
ẓa'iri mada ustesir ma nisī ustammiḥ; the rebellious I rejected, I burned;
the lowly greatly I have strengthened [or the poor I have enriched], and the
people I have rejoiced.—E.I.H. ii. 25.
I now think that ẓa'iri of the first extract is a variant spelling of ẓayari. See p. 338.
ZHP 𒍣𒀪𒉿, zihpi; storehouse. Arabic ﺰَﻌَﻓَ.
𒆠𒄿𒉈𒅎 𒀭 𒍣𒀪𒉿 𒁲𒄭
𒀊𒉌 𒈠 𒍏 𒆠𒆗𒋙 𒀾𒁍 𒊌, kí ṭaim ili zihpi
diṭi abni ma eri kirib-su asbuk; by the command of the god a strong store-
house I built, and metal in it I accumulated.—Neb. Yun. 79.
See parallel passage in p. 224, under Diddi. In that passage I had forgotten
the value of 𒀭𒈠, "myself," and translated "by command of the god,"
instead of "by my own wish." Probably we have the same intention here, and
𒈠 may have been omitted by inadvertence. Read 79 for 71 in the note there. I
find multa accepit in Castell as a value of za'afa in the eighth conjugation.
